quote: Hi. I'm looking for a Chevy. Hi. Is this Wayne?
stewart_read: The opening line is garbled ('looking for a Chevy'), likely a transcription artifact or a rep stumbling over a script line, and the company/reason-for-call framing is delayed until 00:05. This is a rocky start regardless of transcription noise.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be pure diarization/ASR noise rather than a rep error — the phrase doesn't fit any plausible script line.
coaching_implication: Flag for audio review — if the rep actually said something incoherent at open, that's a distinct coaching item from a clean Tesla-intro delivery.

quote: Oh, gotcha. What were you kinda looking into?
stewart_read: After the customer flatly denies wanting solar, the rep doesn't argue or defend — he asks an open question that surfaces the actual product (Powerwall) and de-escalates in one move.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would say the rep was just confused and asking to cover his own gap, not deliberately de-escalating — but the immediate tone shift in the customer's next answers supports the repair reading.
coaching_implication: This is a repeatable move worth reinforcing: when the customer corrects a mismatched assumption, ask rather than assert.

stewart_read: The rep captures the $300 bill figure but immediately moves to closing the call ('Sounds good... that's about all the questions I have here') without reflecting the number back or tying it to the Powerwall/solar conversation.
alternative_hypothesis: Since this is a Powerwall-only inquiry rather than a solar-savings pitch, the bill figure may be less central to the specialist's pitch — but Ion's own bill_anchoring principle treats capture-without-flip as a failure pattern regardless of product.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge the number verbally before moving on — even one line ('$300, got it — that's real money going out every month') sets up the specialist's conversation.

quote: we just need to take a look at just the usage information from a recent Dominion bill.
stewart_read: Rep raises the bill document requirement clearly and pivots smoothly to email once the customer objects to text links — a clean micro-trade that resolves a trust concern without losing the ask.
coaching_implication: This exchange (text declined due to link-safety concern, pivoted to email) is a good example to replay for reps struggling with tech-friction pivots.

quote: the Powerwall, were you wanting to finance or, pay cash for it?
stewart_read: Customer responds 'I don't know, I'll just take a look at what the cost were' — an open payment-method question with no anchor to reason for interest. Rep acknowledges and moves on without probing what's driving the Powerwall interest (backup power, outages, etc.).
alternative_hypothesis: The setter's scope is narrow and payment method may just be a checklist item not meant to open deeper discovery — reactive read is plausible here too.
coaching_implication: A follow-up like 'what's got you looking at battery backup?' would have surfaced the interest reason the script calls for and given the closer a stronger opening.
